ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a combinational logic circuit composed entirely of NOR gates. On the left side there are four two-input NOR gates: the topmost inputs are P and Q; the second inputs are Q and R; the third inputs are P and R; the bottommost inputs are Q and R. The outputs of the upper two left-side NOR gates are connected to an intermediate upper NOR gate; the outputs of the lower two left-side NOR gates are connected to an intermediate lower NOR gate. The outputs of the two intermediate NOR gates are then connected to the final NOR gate on the far right, and the final output is labeled f. Reasoning: Name the four left-side NOR gates according to the connections in the figure: A=(P+Q)', B=(Q+R)', C=(P+R)', D=(Q+R)'. The output of the upper intermediate NOR gate is E=(A+B)', and the output of the lower intermediate NOR gate is G=(C+D)'. The final output is f=(E+G)'. Substitute and simplify: E=((P+Q)'+(Q+R)')'=(P+Q)(Q+R)=Q+PR. G=((P+R)'+(Q+R)')'=(P+R)(Q+R)=R+PQ. Therefore f=(Q+PR+R+PQ)'. Using the absorption law R+PR=R, Q+PQ=Q, obtain f=(Q+R)', that is, the inverse of Q+R.
